widget.instructions: The two arrows are your two walks, tip to tail. Displacement runs from your start to your finish.

stem: You walk {{a}} m east along a straight road, then {{b}} m back west.

hints.text: Where do you finish compared with where you started?
Walking back west undoes part of the eastward walk.
Displacement = final position − initial position, with its direction.

path-length-for-displacement.text: That is the total distance walked, the path length. Displacement compares only where you started and finished.

displacement-sign.text: You finish east of the start, so the displacement points east.

generic.text: Compare only the start and the end of the walk.

workedSolution.text: You end {{a}} − {{b}} = {{net}} m east of where you began.
So the displacement is {{net}} m east, while the path length is {{path}} m.

path-length-for-displacement.front: Is displacement the total distance travelled?
path-length-for-displacement.back: No. Displacement is the change in position (final − initial), with a direction; path length is the total distance covered.

displacement-sign.back: Yes. Its sign gives its direction along the axis: negative means towards −x.

generic.back: Displacement: change in position (with direction). Path length: total distance covered.

accessibility.altText: Two arrows on a grid: {{a}} m to the east, then {{b}} m back to the west.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Choose an answer with the radio buttons; the board only illustrates the walk.
